extracted.intended_audience: public_relations practitioners, journalists, public_information_officers, and media scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for press releases considered as information subsidies to news media — what makes a release more likely to be used by journalists and how subsidies shape news production. Useful for PR writers, PIOs, and researchers studying media sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drop-in ready / reduces journalist workload
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release is more effective as a subsidy if it reduces journalist workload: Pre-written, copy-paste ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides text that requires minimal editing so reporters can quickly adapt it into a story; the release should minimize the reporter's time investment. (Page phrasing: 'Reduces journalist workload: Pre-written, copy-paste ready')

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides everything needed (quotes, data, multimedia, context)
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective subsidy 'provides everything needed' including quotes, data, multimedia, and context so journalists can produce a story without extensive additional reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ready-to-use quotes, key facts, contextual background, charts/graphics and links to datasets so reporters can assemble a piece rapidly. This overlaps with reducing workload but emphasizes comprehensiveness ('Provides everything needed: Quotes, data, multimedia, context').

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of source
rubrics_metrics.description: Comes from a credible source: established institution, known PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases from well-known institutions or recognizable public information officers are more likely to be used because they lower perceived reputational and verification risk. (Page phrasing: 'Comes from credible source: Established institution, known PIO')

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to outlet (beat and audience match)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hits relevance criteria by matching the outlet's beat and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target releases to the specific beats, beats editors, or audiences of an outlet; relevance increases pickup. (Page phrasing: 'Hits relevance criteria: Matches outlet's beat and audience')

rubrics_metrics.name: Saves verification time / includes sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Saves verification time by being pre-fact-checked and providing source links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include citations, links to primary documents, and clear sourcing so journalists spend less time verifying claims. (Page phrasing: 'Saves verification time: Pre-fact-checked, with source links')

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity/differentiation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides exclusivity options: differentiated offers for top outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering embargoes, exclusives, or tailored angles for specific outlets can increase the likelihood of placement among high-value targets. (Page phrasing: 'Provides exclusivity options: Differentiated for top outlets')

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast-ready elements (b-roll, sound bites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes broadcast-ready elements such as b-roll and sound bites to facilitate use in TV/radio segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide video clips, ready-to-use audio bites, and suggested sound-bytes formatted for broadcast to increase uptake by broadcast journalists. (Page phrasing from implicit rubric: 'Includes broadcast-ready elements (b-roll, sound bites)')

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-arranged interviews offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Offers pre-arranged interviews to make it easy for reporters to secure spokespeople.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List available spokespeople, times, and contact details, and offer to schedule interviews to lower friction for reporters ('Pre-arranged interviews offered').

rubrics_metrics.name: Background materials provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides background materials to give reporters context and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include backgrounders, timelines, FAQs, bios, and extended context so reporters can extend a brief item into a fuller story ('Background materials provided').

rubrics_metrics.name: Jargon translated to lay terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Translates jargon into lay terms so the story is accessible to a general audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid technical language or explicitly define terms; provide plain-language explanations to increase utility for general-audience outlets ('Translates jargon to lay terms').

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotable quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides quotable quotes that reporters can readily insert into stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply clear, pithy, attributable quotes that encapsulate the story's angle and are likely to be used verbatim ('Provides quotable quotes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Data offered in multiple formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Offers data in multiple formats to facilitate reuse (e.g., tables, CSV, charts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide machine-readable files, downloadable charts, and embed-ready graphics to reduce the effort required to reproduce figures ('Offers data in multiple formats').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of embargoes for planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Comes with an embargo for planning, allowing journalists to prepare coverage in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State embargo terms clearly (date/time and conditions) to give reporters time to research and schedule stories while controlling timing ('Comes with embargo for planning').

rubrics_metrics.name: Source production capacity / PR infrastructure advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness is shaped by the source's production capacity: elite institutions with PR apparatuses dominate subsidy flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that organizations with dedicated PR resources can produce higher-volume, higher-quality subsidies — a structural advantage noted by Gandy ('Resource-disparate sources, particularly elite institutions with PR apparatuses, dominate subsidy flows'). This is a factor reporters and evaluators should account for when assessing representativeness and diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic effects and biases (agenda bias; churnalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heavy reliance on PR subsidies contributes to agenda bias toward elite interests, decline in original journalism, echo chamber effects, and 'churnalism' (rewriting press releases as news).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat pickup of press-release material as having normative implications for news diversity and quality; editors and journalists should be aware of the risk that reliance on subsidies prioritizes efficiency over independent sourcing and may reproduce elite perspectives ('Agenda bias toward elite interests over grassroots voices', 'Churnalism - rewriting press releases as news').
